headline: Modison, Oberoi Realty and LTM announce cash dividends
summary: Modison, Oberoi Realty and LTM declared dividends with a record date of October 23. Modison will pay ₹4 per share, Oberoi Realty ₹2 per share and LTM ₹25 per share. Modison reported sharply higher Q2FY27 profit and revenue, while Oberoi Realty’s profit rose modestly but its income fell. The payouts provide immediate cash returns to shareholders.

headline: LTM declares Rs 25 dividend as Q2 net profit dips 4% QoQ
hook: Second consecutive quarter of profit contraction
summary: LTM reported a Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 1,397.9 crore, marking a 4% decline compared to the previous quarter. Revenue grew 13.6% year-on-year to reach Rs 11,807.6 crore for the period. The company also announced an interim dividend of Rs 25 per share. Shareholders on record as of October 23, 2026, will be eligible for this payout.
why_it_matters: Dividend payout softens the impact of the sequential profit dip

headline: LTM reports flat Q2 profit of Rs 1,380 crore alongside 14% revenue growth and declares Rs 25 dividend.
hook: Flat profit despite double-digit revenue growth
summary: LTM reported a marginal 0.1% decline in net profit to Rs 1,379.9 crore for the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 13.6% year-on-year to Rs 11,807.6 crore. The company saw strong growth of 47% in its Enterprise AI and Business AI segments. Alongside the financial results, the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 25 per share. Indian retail investors holding LTM shares receive a steady cash payout despite margin pressures offsetting top-line gains.
why_it_matters: Dividend payout offers cash return while flat profit signals margin pressure
winners_losers: LTM shareholders gain / margin-sensitive tech firms hurt

headline: Decoding the recent 11 percent rally in the Nifty IT index over five sessions
hook: IT majors still deep in the red
summary: The Nifty IT index staged an 11 percent recovery over five trading sessions. Despite this recent surge, major IT stocks like Wipro and Infosys remain down 34 percent and 31 percent respectively on a year-to-date basis. LTIMindtree and TCS are also down 29 percent and 26 percent year-to-date. Meanwhile, Tech Mahindra has managed to turn positive for the year following its recent rally.
why_it_matters: Short-term IT stock bounce masks deeper year-to-date losses.
winners_losers: IT investors gain short-term / YTD holders still hurt
